newsitem.title: USA: AT&T says Q3 to see pressure on revs.
newsitem.headline: AT&T says Q3 to see pressure on revs.

text.p: AT&T Corp's third-quarter results will see "pressure on the revenue line" as well as higher costs of sales and marketing, especially in its long-distance business, chief financial officer Richard Miller said.
Call volume has "stabilized," at the second quarter levels, and "we're seeing pressures on the revenue line," Miller said in a telephone conference call with analysts on Tuesday morning.
The call followed AT&T's warning that third quarter share earnings may fall 10 percent below analysts' estimates.
Miller said the company is spending more on marketing. "We're taking more aggressive action on sales and marketing...The core business is still offering a great opportunity for profit."
"We're greatly accelerating our expenditures," chairman Robert Allen said during the call.
Asked by an analyst whether the company would be able to reach its previously stated long-term target of 10 percent earnings growth, Allen said it may occasionally miss the goal.
"There could always be a period the new AT&T will reflect different rates of earnings growth," Allen said.
In the conference call, Allen said the earnings results would fall as much as 10 percent below the "key" analysts' mean estimates of $0.92 per share from operations for the third quarter.
He said the fourth quarter will "likely also fall short" of the "key" mean estimate of $0.89 for the fourth quarter "by roughly comparable amounts."
Asked whether 1997 results would also be lower than analysts expect, Miller said it would be "premature" to talk about next year.

In answer to another question, Allen said the "new" AT&T was "not in an acquisition mode. Not only are we divesting major parts of the old AT&T, but we're divesting other assets not strategic to our future to utilize (capital) and assets in the best possible way."
AT&T is in the midst of splitting into three companies, with AT&T offering calling service, Lucent Technologies Inc offering telecommunications systems and software, and NCR in the computer business.
Allen said AT&T expected to complete distributing the remaining Lucent shares to AT&T holders next week.

Allen said the company has not formally set a long-term earnings goal for the new AT&T. "We well understand what investors expect from the company, and expect earnings growth in that range," Allen said.
Allen said its previously announced three-year jobs reduction plan was "on track," and would lead to about 17,000 job cuts.

ATT officials said in the conference call the company was not ending its various "True Savings" discount programs. "We are not suggesting that every customer will be on one rate," one ATT official said.
AT&T also said on Tuesday that it will offer a single-rate, long-distance calling plan available 24 hours a day. The One Rate plan will offer consumers a flat rate of $0.15 a minute.
In late morning composite trade, AT&T was off 4-3/4 at 52-3/8 on volume of over 8.6 million.
